title: From rule census closure to staged executable readiness
old_model: A complete structured-ID census or completed source review could be read as equivalent to an executable Product rule set.
observed_limitations: Source review can resolve what a passage says while leaving group quantifiers, relation binding, antecedent dependencies, outcome mapping or compiler representation unresolved.
A row-local readiness label can overstate readiness if inherited dependency state is not considered.
Without a separate authorization boundary, semantic-only records could accidentally create runtime effects.
current_model: Track source disposition, semantic closure, Knowledge condition-IR readiness, Product compilation, explicit runtime authorization, internal fidelity and empirical validation as distinct stages. Fail closed when any required stage is unresolved.
rationale: The accepted Career and Response Semantics artifacts make these boundaries operational: 888/888 IDs can coexist with 513 outcome-mapping blockers; 228/228 deep-reviewed blocked rows can coexist with zero compilation/unlock; 26 row-local candidates can yield only 12 Knowledge condition-IR-ready records.
consequences: Preserve denominator and cohort identity in every count.
Do not turn group/quantifier or relation blockers into global defaults.
Treat semantic-only as non-executable absent a separate authorization.
A later compiler or runtime promotion must be a separately versioned, validated event.
what_remains_valid: Deep source review is valuable and can repair source transcription, scope or dependency defects.
Source-first structured representations are a prerequisite for reliable downstream compilation.
Accepted source semantics remain authoritative over Product convenience.

provenance.label: Career blocker ontology backlog — 888 IDs and 513 outcome-mapping blockers

boundaries: This is a project-method boundary derived from accepted artifacts, not a new canonical Zhongzhou rule.
This record does not alter Knowledge or Product runtime semantics.
